newsitem.title: USA: Microchip market to rise 27 pct in 1997 - Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: Microchip market to rise 27 pct in 1997 - Dataquest.

text.p: The worldwide microprocessor market, lead by industry giant Intel Corp, will rise 27 percent to $19.6 billion in 1997, a market researcher said Wednesday.

Intel will continue to be the biggest maker of chips to run personal computers, but smaller chipmakers, such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc and Cyrix Corp, will raise their market share dramatically this year, said Nathan Brookwood, analyst at research firm Dataquest.

AMD on Wednesday will unveil its K6 microprocessor, a chip that the company claims is as fast as Intel's top-of-the-line Pentium Pro chip. With the K6, AMD will grab some of Intel's share of the market, Dataquest said.
"Historically, Intel led its competitors by several years for each (microprocessor) generation, but this gap shrinks significantly" this year, Brookwood said in his report.

Largely based on the demand for AMD's K6, The market for non-Intel microprocessors will grow three-fold to $2.4 billion in 1997 from $722 million in 1996, Dataquest said. Intel's microprocessor sales will rise 16 percent to $17.1 billion from $14.7 billion.
